questions.question: Explain basic solution, feasible solution, basic feasible solution, degenerate and non- / degenerate basic feasible solution, and discuss their importance in linear programming.
questions.solution_html:
• Basic solution: A solution obtained by setting any n variables(among
  • m+n) equal to zero and solving for remaining m variables (2Marks)
  • Feasible solution: A set of variables satisfies the constraints as well as
  • non negative restrictions (2Marks)
  • Basic feasible solution: A basic solution that also satisfies the non neg
  • ativity restrictions.Every BFS is an extreme point of the convex set of
  • feasible solution. (2Marks)
  • Non-degenerate BFS : It is a BFS in which all the m basic variables
  • are positive and the remaining n variables are zero each. (2Marks)
  • Degenerate BFS: It is a BFS in which one or more of the m basic vari
  • ables are equal to zero. (2Marks)
